newsitem.title: USA: American, BA poised to file for U.S. OK on deal.
newsitem.headline: American, BA poised to file for U.S. OK on deal.

text.p: AMR Corp and British Airways Plc are "poised" to formally apply for U.S. approval of their transatlantic alliance, a British Airways spokesman said Thursday.
"We're poised to file the application" for approval from the U.S. Department of Transportation and the Department of Justice, British Airways spokesman John Lampl said Thursday.
British Airways and American Airlines will host a media conference on Friday to make an "important announcement" about the deal.

Lampl said no changes had been made to the alliance proposal, but declined further comment on Friday's media briefing. The media conference will be held at the Capital Hilton in Washington, D.C. at 1000 EST/1500 GMT.

Will Ris, American's vice president of government affairs, Rob Britton, American's managing director of corporate communications, and David Holmes, British Airways' director of corporate resources, will speak at the presentation.
The proposed alliance has sparked strong opposition from U.S. carriers, which contend the massive alliance would limit competition on routes between the United States and London Heathrow airport.

On Thursday, Continental Airlines Inc, Trans World Airlines Inc and UAL Corp's United Airlines spoke out against the alliance. The airlines said BA and American must make concessions to make the competitive situation fair in their view.
BA and American said their proposed alliance will enhance competition, since the deal is contingent on a new Anglo-U.S. air treaty.
